[NAHHAS:v2p161/r8] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The Medinans and Kufans read an taqūlū, while Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Muḥayṣin, ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read an yaqūlū.

[IBNHIBBAN:2247/r2] IBNHIBBAN, d. 354 · معاوية بن الحكم السلمي | reports | After Muʿāwiya spoke to a man during prayer, the Prophet taught that ordinary human speech does not belong in prayer, which consists of glorification, magnification, and Quran recitation.
[IBNHIBBAN:2247/r3] IBNHIBBAN, d. 354 · معاوية بن الحكم السلمي | reports | The repeated account says the Prophet emancipated Muʿāwiya’s maid after she affirmed God’s location in heaven and identified Muhammad as God’s Messenger, taking her affirmation as evidence of faith.
[IBNHIBBAN:6166/r1] IBNHIBBAN, d. 354 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | Umar reports that God drew two groups of descendants from Adam’s back, assigning one to Paradise and the other to Hell, each to act in keeping with that destiny.

[KHATTABI:v1p31/r4] KHATTABI, d. 388 · author | holds | The demonstrative “dhāk” points to something near the speaker, whereas “dhālik” is used for something farther away.

[SULAMI:v1p247#5/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو سعيد الخراز | reports | Abu Sa'id al-Kharraz says believers encountered God in tranquility, recognized Him, and became calm, while unbelievers encountered overwhelming majesty, lost their reason, and scattered from Him.
[SULAMI:v1p247#5/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · يوسف | reports | Yusuf says God addressed them while they existed only through His bringing them into being; they apprehended the Real independently of their own existence, in a way known and found only by Him.
[SULAMI:v1p247#5/r3] SULAMI, d. 412 · بعضهم | reports | Some say the primordial response began without direct witnessing; after unveiling, they witnessed the realities addressed to them and said, 'We bear witness.'
[SULAMI:v1p247#5/r4] SULAMI, d. 412 · الحسين | reports | Al-Husayn says the particles spoke faith willingly and under compulsion; after God showed them His reality, divine power spoke for them without their participation.
[SULAMI:v1p247#5/r5] SULAMI, d. 412 · قيل | reports | A special form of tawhid is for the servant's secret to stand before God while His governance and decrees carry him through unity, effacing the self as the Real sustains him.
[SULAMI:v1p247#5/r6] SULAMI, d. 412 · النصر آباذي | reports | Al-Nasrabadi contrasts an earlier primordial taking with a later appointed taking through lineages, embryos, and clots; the passage's wording is difficult, so the relation is uncertain.
[SULAMI:v1p247#5/r7] SULAMI, d. 412 · النصر آباذي | reports | Al-Nasrabadi says God's taking is not merely tenderness and generosity but majesty, greatness, independence, and self-sufficiency.
[SULAMI:v1p247#5/r8] SULAMI, d. 412 · النصر آباذي | reports | Al-Nasrabadi says the taking was for proof rather than need, and God kept creatures from seeing even a particle of the proof's meanings.
[SULAMI:v1p247#5/r9] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو عثمان المغربي | reports | Abu Uthman al-Maghribi defines creatures as forms on which the decrees of divine power operate, and describes God's taking as moving them from one source or substance to another.
[SULAMI:v1p248/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · الجريري | reports | Al-Jariri says God made Himself known to each group through the knowledge He bestowed, and each affirmed Him; the cited verses say God, not human effort, united hearts. | mentions 3:103, 8:63
[SULAMI:v1p248/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو سعيد الخراز | reports | Al-Kharraz says only divine power, effective decree, and complete will could have answered; the people were merely traces of the Sovereign's decrees, as they remain forms under His governance.
[SULAMI:v1p248/r3] SULAMI, d. 412 · بعضهم | reports | Some call the primordial address a matter of power set forth in the very eye of nonexistence.

[SULAMI:v1p248/r5] SULAMI, d. 412 · قيل | reports | Some say their answer accorded with surrender and was a station of annihilation; the world remains under divine subjection in the grip of the Real.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p475/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | A story says the prophets appeared among the extracted souls like lamps; Adam admired David and gave him forty years from his own thousand-year lifespan, then disputed with the Angel of Death when he died at 960.

[TABRISI:7:172-174/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The covenant was made so people could not plead ignorance or excuse their own shirk by saying their forefathers were polytheists and they merely followed them.

[TABRISI:7:173-174/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · الرماني وأبو مسلم وابن الإخشيد | reports | Likewise, unbelievers “witness against themselves” by manifest conduct though they do not verbally confess unbelief (9:17). | mentions 9:17

[TABRISI:7:173/r12] TABRISI, d. 548 · جماعة من المفسرين | reports | The account says the particles returned to Adam's loins; those who remained Muslim preserved the original fitra, while unbelievers changed from it, supported by both raised and stopped reports.

[RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | Their first objection says the plural phrase from their backs means God took descendants from the backs of Adam's children, never saying He took them from Adam's own back.

[RAZI-FULL:v15p39#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | Their fourth objection says testimony requires rationality, and a rational person could not entirely forget such a momentous event; otherwise one must equally accept reincarnation despite no memory of previous bodies.

[RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | After Moses' story, Razi presents the covenant passage as establishing the proof against all morally responsible people.

[RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · مقاتل | reports | Muqatil says God drew dustlike descendants from Adam, elicited their testimony; the white were destined for paradise by mercy and the black for hell, then all were returned to Adam's loins.

[RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas reports that Adam saw luminous descendants, including the prophets and the especially radiant David; Adam gave David forty years of his own thousand-year lifespan, later denying the gift when death came, after which each lifespan was recorded.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p39/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | rejects | The Mu'tazilites categorically reject interpreting the verse as a literal extraction of progeny and covenant from Adam's descendants.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | Their fifth objection is that the descendants of Adam together would occupy an immense volume that could not fit inside his small back.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | Their sixth objection says bodily structure is necessary for life and reason, and that all descendants with the required bodies could not fit in the earthly space, much less Adam's loins.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p40/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | Their seventh objection asks whether the covenant was proof at the time or later: it could not entail reward or punishment then, and forgotten testimony cannot serve as proof during earthly life.

[RAZI-FULL:v15p41#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | rejects | Rāzī's twelfth objection is that the accountable human is created through the reproductive stages named in scripture, not as primordial particles. | mentions 23:12, 80:17, 80:18

[RAZI-FULL:v15p41/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | Their ninth objection says that if the primordial descendants had full reason and ability, they were already accountable and would need a prior covenant, causing an impossible regress; if not, they could not receive the command.
